'''Rosebys''' was a British retail chain, consisting of over 300 soft-furnishing stores across the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>[http://www.how-do.co.uk/north-west-media-news/north-west-marketing-services/bjl-creates-and-launches-new-rosebys-brand-200712191573/ BJL creates and launches new Rosebys brand], ''How-Do: News, opinion and resources for the North West media industry'', 19 December 2007.  Accessed on line 21 December 2007.</ref> 

Rosebys sold bedding, curtains, bathroom textiles, and other products.<ref>[http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-18238882_ITM Rosebys' boss visit], ''Europe Intelligence Wire'', 14 December 2004.  Accessed on line 21 December 2007.</ref> In September 2008 it was announced that Rosebys had become a victim of the [[Great Recession|recession]] caused by the [[2008 financial crisis]] and had been placed into [[Administration (insolvency)|administration]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jobs fear on Rosebys administration |work=[[The Press Association]] |date=26 September 2008 |access-date=26 September 2008 |url=http://ukpress.google.com/article/ALeqM5i9K9SVWIogipl39cE9Kt39GkWiMQ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081001131204/http://ukpress.google.com/article/ALeqM5i9K9SVWIogipl39cE9Kt39GkWiMQ |archive-date=1 October 2008 }}</ref> 

As of 2024, the defunct brand is still owned by Indian manufacturing company, GHCL Limited, who bought the chain in June 2006.

==History==
[[File:Rosebys and Bensons - Crown Point Retail Park - geograph.org.uk - 1145737.jpg|thumb|right|A Rosebys at Crown Point retail park in [[Leeds]].]]
Rosebys was founded in [[Grimsby]] in 1922 and, following this, expanded into [[Yorkshire]] and northeast [[England]].  They acquired a number of other companies in the 1980s, including Sherrys, Stapleton Linens, Maytime Linens, and Waldmans, and became a publicly traded company in 1992. They acquired Brentfords, Knightingales, Shallets, Russells and Bond Street Fabrics in 1995, Rexmore in 1996, and Bensons Beds, The Fabric Warehouse.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fabricwarehouse.co.uk/the-fabric-warehouse/ |title=The Fabric Warehouse |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151110030103/http://www.fabricwarehouse.co.uk/the-fabric-warehouse/ |archive-date=November 10, 2015 |website=www.fabricwarehouse.co.uk }}</ref> and Fads/Homestyle in 2000. Following this, the company changed its name to Homestyle Group.[[Image:Rosebys, Hounslow, 27-09-08.JPG|thumb|right|A Rosebys' store the day after the group was placed in administration.]]<ref name=au>[http://www.rosebys.com/default.aspx?src=102 About Us], Rosebys.  Accessed on line 21 December 2007.</ref>  Homestyle Group bought the Harveys chain in 2000.<ref>[https://www.telegraph.co.uk/money/main.jhtml?xml=/money/2000/10/20/cxquest.xml The Questor Column]{{dead link|date=July 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, George Trefgarne, ed., telegraph.co.uk.  Accessed on line 21 December 2007.</ref>  Knightingales stores were rebranded as Rosebys in 2002. In 2004, Rosebys and Fabric Warehouse were acquired by [[Lloyds Development Capital]] and split into two separate companies.<ref name=au />  In 2006, Rosebys was acquired by ''Gujarat Heavy Chemicals Ltd.'', part of the [[India]]-based [[Dalmia Group]].<ref>[http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2006/06/20/stories/2006062003870200.htm  GHCL to acquire UK's Rosebys for $40 million], ''The Hindu Business Line'', 20 June 2006.</ref>

== Closure ==
On Friday 26 September 2008, with quarterly rents being due on the following Monday,<ref>{{cite news |first=Julia|last=Kollewe|title=2,000 jobs under threat as textile firm Rosebys goes bust|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2008/sep/26/retail.creditcrunch|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=26 September 2008|access-date=26 September 2008 }}</ref> it was announced that Rosebys had been placed into administration, with the loss of 2,000 jobs. Despite an annual turnover of £100m, the group had become a victim of reduced high street spending with fears that it would be the first of such high street failures. 

In November 2008, [[Edinburgh Woollen Mill]] bought 77 stores from the administrators and merged them with the assets of furnishings business [[Ponden Home|Ponden Mill]] to create the 150-strong [[Ponden Home]] chain.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-17170281 New owner could reopen 75 Peacocks stores], ''BBC News - Wales'', 26 February 2012.</ref>
